text: I would say every single time the voice in your head is wrong. That critical voice in your head. To be specific, I'm talking about the voice in your head that is critical and repeats.
speaker: Joe Hudson
context: Lenny asks Joe about his insight that the voice in your head is often wrong and contradictory. Joe explains that the critical, repetitive voice in your head - the one that constantly tells you things like "you should work out more" - is always wrong, even when there might be some truth to what it's saying. He argues that this voice isn't actually helping you be productive, despite what most people believe.
text_ko: 제 생각엔 머릿속의 목소리는 매번 틀려요. 그건 바로 비판적이고 되풀이되는 머릿속의 목소리(critical voice)를 말하는 거예요.
text_zh: 我想说的是，你脑子里那个声音每次都不对——就是那个不停批评你、老在脑子里反复回放的声音。
text_es: Yo diría que, siempre que aparece, la vocecita crítica en tu cabeza está equivocada. Para ser más claro: me refiero a esa voz que te critica y no deja de repetirse.
key_sentence: The critical voice in your head is always wrong and repeats itself.
original_text: I would say every single time the voice in your head is wrong. That critical voice in your head. To be specific, I'm talking about the voice in your head that is critical and repeats. There's the voice that says the same thing over and over again. You got to work out more, you got to work out more, you got to work out more. Whatever that is, it's always wrong, and that doesn't mean there isn't truth to what it says, but it's incorrect.

vocabulary.definition: Expressing adverse or disapproving comments or judgments; essential for the success or functioning of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a 'critical' analysis can reveal weaknesses in a strategy, while critical feedback is vital for employee development and performance improvement.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'critical' can imply negativity, in a business context, it often refers to necessary evaluations that drive improvement.

text: I think the best way to work with the voice in the head is to pick an experiment every day and respond to the voice in the head in a new way every day.
speaker: Joe Hudson
context: Lenny asks Joe how to practically work with the critical voice in your head. Joe explains that instead of trying to stop or control this voice, you should change how you relate to it. He recommends taking an experimental approach where you respond to the critical voice differently each day, treating it like a scared child rather than an authority figure.
text_ko: 제 생각엔 머릿속의 목소리와 잘 일하려면 매일 하나씩 실험을 정해서 그 목소리에 매번 새롭게 반응해 보는 게 좋아요.
text_zh: 我觉得跟脑子里的那个声音打交道，最好的办法是每天做个小实验，每天用不一样的方式去回应它。
text_es: Creo que la mejor manera de manejar la voz interior es probar un experimento distinto cada día y responderle de una forma nueva cada vez.
key_sentence: Pick an experiment daily to respond to the voice in your head.
original_text: I think the best way to work with the voice in the head is to pick an experiment every day and respond to the voice in the head in a new way every day. One of my favorite responses is, "Oh, I see that you're really scared. Don't worry. I'm right here with you. I got you."

vocabulary.definition: A systematic procedure undertaken to make a discovery or test a hypothesis.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, experiments are often used in product development and marketing to test new ideas and measure their effectiveness before full-scale implementation.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'experiment' implies a methodical approach to testing, it can also suggest a degree of uncertainty or risk, making it less suitable in contexts where certainty is expected.

vocabulary.definition: To react or reply to a stimulus, question, or situation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, responding effectively to customer feedback or market changes is crucial for maintaining competitive advantage and customer satisfaction.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'respond' carries a connotation of active engagement, suggesting that the response is thoughtful rather than merely reactive.

text: It's such an important tool for productivity. If you say, I'm going to figure out how to enjoy what I do 10% more and you succeed, you are 10% more efficient. Not only that, usually, the quality is going to get a lot better too.
speaker: Joe Hudson
context: Lenny asks Joe about his focus on helping people feel joy. Joe explains that enjoyment isn't just about feeling good - it's actually a powerful productivity tool. He argues that if you can learn to enjoy what you're doing even 10% more, you become 10% more efficient and the quality of your work improves significantly.
text_ko: 정말 생산성(productivity)을 높이는 중요한 도구예요. ‘내가 하는 일을 10% 더 즐기게 만드는 방법을 찾아볼 거야’라고 생각해서 실제로 그렇게 된다면 10% 더 효율적으로 일하게 돼요. 게다가 보통 일의 품질도 훨씬 좋아져요.
text_zh: 这真的是提高工作效率的重要手段。你要是能想办法让自己对工作多享受个10%，那你的效率就能提升10%。不仅如此，通常工作质量也会大幅提升。
text_es: Es una herramienta clave para la productividad. Si te dices, voy a buscar la manera de disfrutar 10% más lo que hago y lo logras, vas a ser 10% más eficiente. Y no solo eso, por lo general la calidad también va a mejorar muchísimo.
key_sentence: Enjoying what you do 10% more is a tool for productivity.

vocabulary.definition: Productivity refers to the efficiency with which goods and services are produced, often measured as the output per unit of input over a specific period.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, productivity is a key performance indicator that helps organizations assess their operational efficiency and workforce effectiveness.
vocabulary.nuance: While often associated with quantitative measures, productivity can also encompass qualitative aspects, such as employee satisfaction and innovation.

vocabulary.definition: Efficient describes the ability to achieve maximum productivity with minimum wasted effort or expense.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startup settings, being efficient is crucial for resource allocation, ensuring that time and capital are utilized effectively to drive growth.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often implies a balance between speed and quality, suggesting that efficiency should not compromise the overall outcome.

vocabulary.definition: Quality refers to the standard of something as measured against other things of a similar kind; it encompasses the degree of excellence or superiority.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, maintaining high quality is essential for customer satisfaction and brand reputation, often influencing competitive advantage.
vocabulary.nuance: Quality can be subjective and varies across industries; thus, it is important to define specific quality metrics relevant to the context.

text: Whatever emotion that you're trying to avoid, you are inviting into your life in exactly the way that you're trying to avoid it.
speaker: Joe Hudson
context: Lenny asks Joe what is holding people back from success and living the life they want. Joe identifies emotions that people are not sitting with, feeling, or expressing as a major factor. He explains a counterintuitive principle: when you try to avoid feeling a particular emotion, you actually end up experiencing more of that exact emotion in your life.
text_ko: 피하려고 애쓰는 감정일수록, 오히려 그걸 피하려는 바로 그 방식대로 삶에 초대하고 있어요.
text_zh: 你越想逃避什么情绪，它就越会以你最不想要的方式出现在你生活里。
text_es: Cualquier emoción que trates de evitar, la estás invitando a tu vida justo de la manera en que intentas evitarla.
key_sentence: Avoided emotions are inviting into your life in exactly the way you resist.

vocabulary.definition: Welcoming or appealing, often in a way that encourages participation or engagement.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'inviting' can refer to creating an environment or atmosphere that encourages collaboration, innovation, or customer engagement.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'inviting' generally has positive connotations, it can imply a degree of vulnerability when discussing emotional or personal matters.

vocabulary.definition: A complex psychological state that involves a subjective experience, physiological response, and behavioral or expressive response.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding emotion is crucial for effective marketing, customer service, and team dynamics, as it influences decision-making and consumer behavior.
vocabulary.nuance: While often associated with personal feelings, in a business context, emotions can also drive motivation and engagement; however, they should be managed carefully to maintain professionalism.

text: A lot of the people in my circles may have spent hundreds of millions of dollars to try to arrange a life that they enjoy, and it doesn't fucking work.
speaker: Joe Hudson
context: Joe is explaining why learning to enjoy what you're currently doing is more powerful than trying to arrange your external circumstances for enjoyment. He notes that many wealthy people he coaches have spent enormous amounts of money trying to create an enjoyable life through external means - buying jets, islands, and luxury items - but this approach fundamentally fails to create lasting satisfaction.
text_ko: 제 주변 사람들 중 많은 분들이 자기들이 즐길 수 있는 삶을 만들기 위해 수억 달러를 썼을 수도 있는데, 그게 진짜 아무 소용이 없더라고요.
text_zh: 我身边很多人砸了几个亿想要打造自己理想的生活，结果根本不管用。
text_es: Muchos de la gente en mi entorno han gastado cientos de millones de dólares tratando de armar una vida que les guste, y no funciona para nada.
key_sentence: Arranging a life often doesn't fucking work, despite spending millions.

vocabulary.definition: To organize or make plans for something in a systematic way.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'arrange' often refers to the coordination of meetings, events, or resources to achieve specific objectives.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'arrange' implies a level of planning and order, it may also suggest flexibility in adapting to changing circumstances.

vocabulary.definition: To take pleasure in or derive satisfaction from an experience or activity.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of employee engagement, 'enjoy' can refer to the satisfaction derived from workplace culture, benefits, or job roles that enhance productivity.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'enjoy' conveys a positive experience, it may not always imply fulfillment or long-term happiness, especially in a professional context.

text: I would do seven minutes, no less than seven minutes. You can do more than seven minutes. Seven minutes of gratitude with another person every day.
speaker: Joe Hudson
context: Lenny asks Joe for one practical thing everyone can try to become better and more successful. Joe recommends a specific daily gratitude practice: spending exactly seven minutes sharing gratitude back and forth with another person, but emphasizing that it must come from actually feeling the emotion of gratitude in your body, not just intellectual thoughts about what you're grateful for.
text_ko: 저라면 일곱 분은 꼭 하겠어요. 그보다 짧게는 하지 말고, 더 길게 하셔도 돼요. 매일 다른 사람과 일곱 분 동안 감사의 시간을 가져보세요.
text_zh: 我建议至少七分钟，别少于七分钟。可以更久。每天和别人一起花七分钟做感恩练习。
text_es: Te recomendaría siete minutos, no menos. Puedes dedicar más tiempo si quieres, pero procura tener siete minutos diarios de gratitud con otra persona.
key_sentence: Practice seven minutes of gratitude back and forth with another person.
original_text: I would do seven minutes, no less than seven minutes. You can do more than seven minutes. Seven minutes of gratitude with another person every day. It has to be feeling the gratitude and then seeing what comes out of your mouth when you're coming from the felt sense of gratitude and doing it back and forth.

vocabulary.definition: A feeling of thankfulness and appreciation, often expressed towards others for their support or contributions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, expressing gratitude can enhance workplace relationships, boost morale, and foster a positive organizational culture.
vocabulary.nuance: Gratitude carries a positive connotation and is often associated with emotional intelligence and leadership effectiveness.

text: Joy is the matriarch of a family of emotions and she won't come into a house where her children aren't welcome. A very joyful life is a life where all the other emotions are deeply welcomed, not accepted, not non-judgmentally aware of.
speaker: Joe Hudson
context: Lenny asks Joe about the difference between non-judgmental awareness of emotions (from meditation practices) and Joe's approach to working with emotions. Joe shares his famous metaphor about joy being like the matriarch of a family - she won't visit a home where her children (other emotions) aren't truly welcome. He emphasizes that emotions need to be welcomed and loved, not just tolerated or observed neutrally.
text_ko: 기쁨은 감정들의 어머니 같은 존재예요. 그 감정들이 환영받지 못하는 집에는 기쁨이 들어오지 않아요. 진정으로 기쁨이 넘치는 삶은 다른 모든 감정들을 단순히 받아들이거나 판단하지 않는 정도로 알아주는 게 아니라, 깊이 마음으로 환영하는 삶이에요.
text_zh: 快乐就像是情绪大家庭里的老大，如果她的孩子们在这个家里不受欢迎，她是不会进门的。真正快乐的人生，就是要发自内心地拥抱所有其他的情绪，不是简单地接受，也不是那种无所谓的态度。
text_es: La alegría es como la matriarca de toda la familia de emociones, y no va a entrar a una casa donde sus hijos no sean bienvenidos. Una vida realmente plena es aquella donde todas las demás emociones son profundamente bienvenidas, no solo aceptadas o reconocidas sin más.
key_sentence: Joy is the matriarch of a family of emotions, welcomed deeply in life.

vocabulary.definition: Regarded as valid, recognized, or approved by a group or community.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, accepted practices or standards are those that are widely endorsed and followed within an industry, influencing operational procedures and strategic decisions.
vocabulary.nuance: The term suggests a level of consensus or agreement, but it may also imply a lack of critical evaluation, which can be problematic in rapidly changing environments.
